ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Finding a precipitant

A 58-year-old man with cirrhosis develops confusion and asterixis after several days of constipation. Glucose is normal and there is no focal weakness. Alongside evaluating other causes of altered consciousness, which factor is a plausible precipitant of hepatic encephalopathy?

  1. Resolution of an infection
  2. Constipation
  3. Improved adherence to prescribed lactulose
  4. Successful control of gastrointestinal bleeding
  5. Correction of hypokalemia
Answer and explanation

Constipation

Reduced intestinal clearance of nitrogenous material can precipitate HE in a susceptible patient.

Option explanations

Constipation: Reduced intestinal clearance of nitrogenous material can precipitate HE in a susceptible patient.

Improved adherence to prescribed lactulose: Appropriate lactulose use generally helps prevent recurrence.

Successful control of gastrointestinal bleeding: Controlling bleeding removes a potential precipitant.

Correction of hypokalemia: Correcting an electrolyte trigger generally reduces risk.

Resolution of an infection: Treating infection removes another common trigger.
